references.text: Psalm 41:9 mentions that a friend who eats my bread lifts his heel against me, a direct parallel to Jesus' warning that one of his closest disciples would betray him.

Matthew 26:21-24 repeats the same moment where Jesus is troubled in spirit and confirms that one of the twelve will betray him, using the same wording that it would be better for the one who betrays him.
Mark 14:18-21 records Jesus' distress and the direct confirmation that one of the disciples will betray him, focusing on the fact that it is one of the twelve who shares bread with him.

Luke 22:21-22 describes Jesus warning about the betrayal by saying that the hand of the one who betrays him is at the table with him, and emphasizes that the Son of Man goes as it has been determined.
